To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the production of indol alkaloids in immobilized C. roseus cultures is enhanced if the production stage is preceded by a growth stage in a medium containing IAA instead of 2,4-D, and if the growth stage is performed at a late exponential phase.

(i) immobilized cultures produced higher yields of known indole alkaloids and released more of them than suspension cultures, (ii) 2-stage culture regime yielded higher total alkaloid production, (iii) the production stage in the 2-stage regime should be initiated in late exponential phase of growth, and (iv) 2,4- dichlorophenoxy acetic acid should not be included in the growth stage.
2-stage surface-immobilized C. roseus cultures produced more known alkaloids at higher yields and released more alkaloids in the medium than 1-stage surface-immobilization cultures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of bioreactor cultures for the production of known indole alkaloids by C. roseus cells.
the evaluation of the effects of immobilization on the production of indoles by C. roseus cells.
the optimization of the production process of Catharanthus alkaloids by immobilized cultures, using a bioreactor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
immobilized cultures are more productive than suspension cultures, but the latter produce more alkaloids.
the 2-stage immobilization process is not a good process for production of indole-alkaloids by C. roseus cells.
the immobilized culture process is a promising tool for alkaloid production by C. roseus, but that it is still in need of improvement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

immobilized cultures of C. roseus cells, when grown in a bioreactor and according to the 2-stage regime, produced 2 to 5 times more known alkaloids and 3 to 10 times more unknowns, as compared to shake flask cultures.
the use of 2 l immobilization bioreactors for alkaloid production is feasible, although the use of 200 ml shake flasks may be preferable, especially for the production of known indole alkaloids.

the 2-stage immobilization process is a promising approach for the production of known alkaloids by C. roseus cells, provided that the culture is performed at the optimal stage of growth, in the presence of the appropriate growth regulator and in the absence of aeration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
2-stage immobilization is a viable alternative for the production of known indole alkaloids by Catharanthus cells.

the immobilized 2-stage culture process, although it is not as productive as 2-stage suspension culture process, can be used to study the effect of the culture conditions and medium composition on alkaloid production.
2-stage immobilised cultures of Catharanthous roseus are more productive than 2-stage suspension culture, and the 2-stage immobilisation process is more productive than 1-stage immobilized cultures.
